source: tools/list capture over 1,749 credential-less (OPEN) endpoints from the public MarketNow catalog

positive_set.definition: tool name matches a read-verb prefix AND description contains tier keywords (co-occurrence candidates for tuning, NOT verdicts)
positive_set.read_name_rule: name (case-insensitive) starts with a read verb followed by '_', '-', a digit, an uppercase letter (camelCase), or end-of-name; manual check because IGNORECASE breaks character-class boundaries

B_protocol.amendment: Definition pinned 2026-10-05 (it was previously only implied). Reconciliation of the 24 vs 27 discrepancy from the audit: the published tier B contains only uppercase POST (23 tools) and PUT (1) matches — the analyzer silently excluded the uppercase DELETE/PATCH population on read-named tools (re-measured: 7 further instances, e.g. get_events, list_schedules, list_verified_numbers, lookup_program, inspect_requests, read_file, get_device_egress_fail_posture). Counted against the 4-verb uppercase set with word boundaries, the read-named population is 27-31 depending on the read-name boundary rule (camelCase check). The audit's 27 is the defensible count; 24 was a filter artifact, not a disagreement.

comma_gap.definition: descriptions where a read-verb lead is followed by a comma and a state-change verb inside the same sentence (the #101 reproduction population)
comma_gap.amendment: The published figures (36 tools / 10 read-named) came from the capture-session analyzer, whose exact boundary implementation was lost with the session; the definition as stated is not tight enough to reimplement (sentence segmentation and 'read-verb lead' interpretation are both underspecified). The audit's independent reconstruction over this same corpus yields 63 candidates / 56 read-named. The operative number is the audit's: of the 127 would-fire under MCP010 as designed, only 4 are driven by a read lead carrying a comma — a 3% effect on a 99.2% false-positive problem. Comma examples below are illustrative, not a sized population; 6 of the original 8 examples do not have byte-identical descriptions in the corpus (truncated at 2,000 chars).

case_sensitivity.definition: names whose lowercase form matches a POSIX-sensitive deny pattern (delete_*, drop_*, ...) but whose actual casing lets them sail past fnmatch
case_sensitivity.amendment: Corrected 2026-10-05 after audit. The 939 tool names and the 69,098 server-name population are the L1 CATALOG populations (70,510 indexed skills), NOT this corpus capture (16,015 tools / 1,648 captured server names) — provenance was mixed in the write-up. Additionally, the 4 example tool names match the stated patterns (delete_*, drop_*) in NEITHER case because of the underscore; they only bypass case-sensitive fnmatch under the broader prefix families (delete*, run*). The audit's defensible count on this corpus is 2 mixed-case, not 4. The hole is real (case-sensitive fnmatch lets DeleteSubgraph past delete*); the numbers behind it are catalog-side, not corpus-side.

tools.population_provenance: L1 catalog (70,510 skills) — not the corpus capture
tools.pattern_family_caveat: delete_*/drop_* match in neither case (underscore); valid only under delete*/run*

server_names.population_provenance: L1 catalog server names — not the corpus capture (1,648 captured)

verification.reprobe: POST {endpoint} with JSON-RPC initialize + tools/list; see README.md

description_case_integrity.question: Audit note: 'one description in the corpus arrives already lowercased (get_generation_request, get_events, get_skill) ... worth knowing before anyone diffs corpus text against live text.'
findings: corpus.jsonl stores descriptions verbatim — case preserved at capture; 97/16,015 descriptions naturally start lowercase (server-side style, e.g. jojapi.com 'search-communities Billing per call: 1 Credits.')

All 12 corpus instances of get_generation_request / get_events / get_skill start with an uppercase letter; zero (name -> description) pairs differ only by casing anywhere in the corpus (0 case-variant duplicates across 1,053 multi-instance names)
Live re-probe 2026-10-05 of all 11 reachable serving endpoints (initialize + tools/list, no tools/call): descriptions byte-identical to the corpus, casing preserved, 11/11

The production matcher lowercases descriptions at entry: mcp_guard/parser.py _detect_destructive and _detect_write both do desc = data.get('description', '').lower() — any lowercased text seen in an adjudication quoting production output comes from the matcher, not from the capture or the servers
Conclusion: corpus-vs-live text diffs are safe with respect to casing; lowercase enters at mcp-guard's match time, not in this artifact

amendments.summary: Integrity of the artifact was verified 100% by the auditor (sha256 exact, 1,656/1,656 frame hashes, positives provenance byte-identical, 4/4 live re-probe). Three write-up claims did not survive verification and are corrected here; two audit side-notes are resolved by new measurements. The data files (corpus.jsonl, frames/, positives.json) are unchanged — corpus.jsonl sha256 remains 5877a249da294430a93322d8ec34dce49391329b0baf5a2195c487d2ac7e9217.

corrections.claim: 'get_recent_transactions / POST /transactions/search is present as a live endpoint in the corpus'
corrections.detail: 0 occurrences of get_recent_transactions, /transactions/search and POST /transactions in corpus.jsonl and in all 1,656 frames (re-verified by grep on 2026-10-05). The case is a level-1 catalog example (the #101 motivation table), not a captured endpoint. The transport-verb caution stands on its structural argument, not on this corpus.

corrections.claim: comma gap: 36 tools, 10 of them read-named
corrections.detail: Definition not reimplementable as stated; analyzer implementation lost with the capture session. Audit reconstruction: 63 candidates / 56 read-named. Operative number: 4 of 127 would-fire driven by a comma (audit). See comma_gap block.

corrections.claim: fnmatch case-sensitivity: 4 of 939 tools, 2 of 198 server names
corrections.detail: Both populations are L1 catalog (70,510 skills / 69,098 server names), not the 16,015-tool capture; presented inside a corpus write-up in error. The 4 examples match the stated underscore patterns in neither case (audit); on this corpus the defensible count is 2 mixed-case. See case_sensitivity block.

resolutions: B_protocol 24 vs 27 reconciled: published tier matched only uppercase POST/PUT (filter artifact); the 4-verb word-boundary count is 27 (audit) / 27-31 (our re-measure, read-name boundary dependent). Definition now pinned in tiers.B_protocol.

Lowercased-descriptions note resolved: capture is verbatim, 11/11 live re-probes byte-identical with casing preserved, 0 case-variant duplicates corpus-wide; lowercase text originates in mcp-guard's matcher (parser.py lowers descriptions in _detect_destructive/_detect_write). See description_case_integrity block.

rejected_example.claim: 'get_*_coinbase_pay_link tools ... the real MCP010 shape' (genuine candidate)
rejected_example.detail: The audit quotes the three descriptions' own disclaimers ('This tool charges nothing by itself', 'read-only: it accepts no email or payment data and cannot complete a purchase', purchase happens on status 'completed'). It creates a link; it does not perform the purchase; production keyword sets score it zero destructive / zero exec. The one genuine positive found by the audit: check_in_attendee (a real write under a check_ name, 1 of 123).
